We're ramping to a paid pilot (two-week launch window) and expect a 2–3x short-duration spike around the campaign that follows. A few questions up front so we can line procurement up:

- What eviction / preemption behavior should we expect if burst uses shared capacity?
- Can you give a templated capacity split (baseline vs burst) you typically recommend for customers with our profile?

We want a concrete template and a short SLA/ops note to share with our infra/procurement team before the 90-day pilot. Happy to take a 30-min run-through this week.

Alex —

Appreciate the sample — that helps a lot. High-level proposal below; I'll loop in the serving/infra owners (cc'd) to confirm feasibility and put a short templated doc together. I've attached a draft SLA + burst clause for initial review (proposal_sla_soft-burst_v1.pdf).

Summary proposal (pilot-focused):
- Baseline (reserved) slab: sized to cover the 60th percentile of sustained peak in the CSV (we'll run numbers in the template).
- Soft-burst pool: ephemeral shared capacity that can be used for short spikes up to 2–3x baseline for short windows (we limit per-customer sustained burst to avoid noisy neighbors).
- Billing: burst usage billed at a multiplier (our standard pilot multiplier is 1.4x per token/VM-hour above reserved), with an option to convert to committed capacity if sustained beyond the pilot window.
- Eviction / preemption: soft-burst is preemptible; Redwood will try graceful draining (prefix caching preserved where possible) and failover to a smaller hosted model variant if preempted. We commit to 30s of graceful handoff for in-flight requests in the SLA draft.
- Autoscale policy recommendations: 60s cool-down, max burst concurrency per region, and a per-customer cap equal to 40% of total effective capacity (configurable).

Next steps: Rishi will sketch concrete GPU sizing (instance types + headroom formula) and Marissa will draft the formal templated worksheet. Can we schedule 30 min tomorrow for an ops walkthrough? Also please confirm procurement timeline for the 90-day pilot and the nominal committed rate you expect.

Folks —

A few concrete, technical guardrails to include in the template and SLA. I ran a quick pass against the CSV; below are conservative suggestions that work across A100/H100 fleets.

1) GPU instance selection + packing
- Preferred: A100 80GB for cost predictability; H100 where latency-sensitive models need faster core performance.
- Typical packing: 1.6x effective model concurrency per A100 when using mixed-precision quantization and continuous batching.

2) Sizing heuristics (quick formulas)
- steady_reserve = ceil(avg_1h_peak * 0.6)
- soft_burst_cap = min(ceil(peak_5m - steady_reserve), ceil(total_reserved * 0.4))
- buffer_pool = max(1, ceil(steady_reserve * 0.1)) // warm KV cache + headroom

Example (from the CSV sample): if 1h avg peak ~= 18 concurrent streams -> steady_reserve = 11 GPUs, soft_burst_cap = min(ceil(32 - 11)=21, ceil(11*0.4)=5) -> recommend capping burst at 5 GPUs for pilot (avoid noisy neighbor exposure).

3) Autoscaling and preemption behavior
- Scale-up: immediate allocation from soft-burst pool (subject to pool caps).
- Scale-down/cooldown: 60s to allow prefix/KV cache persistence.
- Preemption: LRU-based preemption across soft-burst consumers; customers with active canaries or A/B rollouts get priority knobs.

4) Operational notes
- Warmers: schedule KV warmers 2–5 minutes before known campaigns; pre-warming reduces peak tail latency dramatically.
- Monitoring: per-route token rate + GPU utilization alerts; automated rollback to hosted variant if tail latency > SLA for more than 2 minutes.

I'll produce a 1-page technical appendix with these numbers and the sample calculation for Marissa to drop into the customer-facing worksheet.

-rishi
